newsitem.title: USA: Host CEO comfortable with '97 estimates.
newsitem.headline: Host CEO comfortable with '97 estimates.

text.p: Host Marriott Corp Chief Executive and President Terence Golden said he was "generally comfortable" with analysts' EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization) projections of around $625 million for 1997.
"I think we're generally comfortable with it," he told Reuters at the Montgomery Securities Hospitality Conference in New York.
Earlier in the day the company announced a EBITDA figure for 1996 of $442 million versus $311 million in 1995.
Golden said that the company had completed over $1.5 billion worth of acquisitions in 1996 and was targetting more than $1 billion in acquisitions for 1997.
He also said that the pricing at which Host Marriott has been acquiring properties "has been very clearly accretive."

The company announced last week it had acquired the Ritz-Carlton of Marina del Rey, Calif., for $56.6 million. According to a Bankers Trust research report the purchase price of $185,000 per room was about 70 percent of the property's original contruction cost of $275,000 per room.

Golden said that while the company would be open to any attractive acquisition opportunities, its primary focus would remain in the United States. Ten percent of the company's assets are currently outside the United States.
Golden was positive about trends for full-service hotels. "We see the outlook for the intermediate term as being very favorable," he said.
